title: Mechanics: Forces and Motion - Assessment Exam
instructions: Answer all questions. Show all work for calculations. Multiple-choice questions have four options (A, B, C, D). This is a comprehensive assessment of your understanding of mechanics, forces, and motion.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes Newton's first law of motion?
options: An object at rest stays at rest unless acted upon by a net external force
For every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction
Inertia is proportional to an object's weight
questions.explanation: This is the definition of Newton's first law, also known as the law of inertia.

questions.question: A 3 kg object accelerates at 8 m/s² when a net force is applied. What is the magnitude of this net force?
questions.explanation: Using F = ma: F = 3 kg × 8 m/s² = 24 N

questions.question: A book rests on a table. The table exerts an upward normal force on the book. According to Newton's third law, the reaction to this force is:
options: The weight of the book pushing down on the table
The book pushing down on the table
The gravitational force pulling the book toward Earth
Air resistance pushing against the book
questions.explanation: The reaction to the normal force (table pushing up on book) is the book pushing down on the table. Both forces are contact forces between the same two objects.

questions.question: An object is thrown upward at 30 m/s from ground level. At what point is its vertical velocity zero?
options: The vertical velocity is never zero
questions.explanation: At maximum height, the vertical velocity momentarily becomes zero as the object stops rising before beginning to fall.

questions.question: A ball rolls off a 20 m cliff with an initial horizontal velocity of 10 m/s. Which component of velocity changes during the fall?
options: Both horizontal and vertical velocities change equally
Neither horizontal nor vertical velocity changes
questions.explanation: Only the vertical velocity changes due to gravity. The horizontal velocity remains constant because no horizontal forces act on the ball (ignoring air resistance).

questions.question: A 400 N weight is placed 1 m to the left of a pivot on a seesaw. To balance it, a 500 N weight must be placed at what distance to the right?
questions.explanation: Using torque balance: 400 × 1 = 500 × d, so d = 400/500 = 0.8 m. Let me verify: 400 × 1 = 400 N·m, and 500 × 0.8 = 400 N·m. Yes, this is correct. The answer should be 0.8 m, which is option 1.

questions.question: A car travels from rest and reaches a velocity of 24 m/s after 6 seconds with uniform acceleration. What is the acceleration?
Two forces of 6 N and 8 N act perpendicular to each other on an object. What is the magnitude of the resultant force?
A projectile is launched at 40 m/s at 60° above the horizontal. What is its vertical velocity component at launch?
The kinematic equation v² = v₀² + 2as is most useful when you know all variables except:
questions.explanation: This equation relates v, v₀, a, and s, but does not involve time. Use this when you need to find one of these four variables but don't know time.

questions.question: True or False: A freely falling object has zero acceleration.
questions.explanation: A freely falling object has a constant downward acceleration of g ≈ 9.8 m/s² due to gravity.

questions.question: True or False: If the net force on an object is zero, the object must be at rest.
questions.explanation: If net force is zero, the object is in equilibrium, which means it could be at rest OR moving at constant velocity. Both satisfy Newton's first law.

questions.question: True or False: Torque depends only on the magnitude of the force applied.
questions.explanation: Torque depends on both the magnitude of the force AND the perpendicular distance from the pivot to the line of action of the force: τ = F × d.

questions.question: True or False: Mass and weight are the same quantity with different units.
questions.explanation: Mass (kg) is the amount of matter. Weight (N) is the gravitational force on that mass. Weight = mg, so they are related but different quantities.

questions.question: A 2 kg object is dropped from rest. After 3 seconds, its velocity is ________ m/s. (Use g = 10 m/s²)
A ball is thrown horizontally at 15 m/s from a tall building. Its horizontal velocity at maximum height is ________ m/s.
questions.explanation: Horizontal velocity remains constant throughout projectile motion; it is not affected by gravity. At maximum height, vₓ = 15 m/s.

questions.question: A 50 N force is applied at 3 m from a pivot on one side. A 30 N force must be applied at ________ m on the other side to balance the lever.
questions.explanation: Using τ balance: 50 × 3 = 30 × d, so d = 150/30 = 5 m

questions.question: An object accelerates uniformly from 5 m/s to 15 m/s over a distance of 40 m. Its acceleration is ________ m/s².
questions.explanation: Using v² = v₀² + 2as: 15² = 5² + 2a(40), so 225 = 25 + 80a, thus 80a = 200, and a = 2.5 m/s²

questions.question: A 1500 kg car accelerates from rest to 20 m/s in 8 seconds on a horizontal road. Assuming uniform acceleration, calculate the net force acting on the car. Show your work.
A ball is launched at 50 m/s at an angle of 30° above horizontal. Explain why the speed at maximum height is not zero, and calculate this speed. (Hint: cos 30° ≈ 0.866)
questions.correctAnswer: At max height, vertical velocity is zero but horizontal velocity is not. vₓ = 50 cos(30°) = 50 × 0.866 = 43.3 m/s. Speed at max height ≈ 43.3 m/s.
